A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 11 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite renaming and substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original QE evaluations across translation, summarization and question answering, plus token-distribution analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original QE experiments, human token-validity annotations, additional baseline comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: DMP is renamed BOOSTEDPROB, but dominant-token selection, significant-drop thresholds and probability-mass scoring retain the same procedure (v1 Section 3.2; v2 Section 4). Appendix B.2 tests alternative aggregation rules but explicitly retains mean aggregation.

E1.justification: Translation coverage expands beyond English-German: ParaCrawl and WMT22 add Chinese-English, and HJQE adds English-Chinese. Appendix E adds ASR quality-estimation evaluation, whereas v1 used ASR for token-distribution diagnostics. Fleurs cmn-en becoming zh-en is a relabeling.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated Monte Carlo sequence entropy comparisons across several tasks (Table 4) and Perturbation-based QE for HJQE (Table 6). These comparisons were absent from v1. Probability, entropy, CometKiwi and the existing cluster-selection comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 replaces task-specific hyperparameters with shared x=30% and epsilon=0.005, removes Scratch, adds NLLB/Tower, and replaces Scratch/DeltaLM forced-decoding scorers with Prism/NLLB and original HJQE models. New protocols include a 50-sample, two-annotator study, ROUGE-L/BERTScore evaluation and WER-based ASR evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds human validation of dominant tokens, hyperparameter sensitivity plots, aggregation ablations, alternative-metric checks and an ASR applicability test (Appendices A-C and E). The cluster-selection ablation is revised for different scorers and languages. The weak-model hallucination example is retained from v1 and relocated to Appendix D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added human-study averages and token distributions are descriptive results without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 3 removes Scratch and ParaCrawl test rows, adds translation results and revises retained entries, including GSM8K/Llama3.3 from 0.341 to 0.006 for the proposed QE score. The reported average advantage over probability changes from +0.208 to +0.194 across different configurations. v2 also adds baseline, annotation, aggregation, alternative-metric and ASR results; these changes do not establish a controlled performance gain or loss.

T1.justification: The sorting, significant-drop, cutoff and QE equations are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2's added threshold explanations do not introduce substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central underconfidence explanation and inexpensive QE contribution remain. v2 extends headline competitiveness claims to ensemble methods in certain settings and promotes the previously discussed model-quality/QE relationship into an explicit contribution about self-evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of aggregation behavior, BERTScore's difficulty with numerical QA and the practical usefulness of modest correlations. It recommends stronger external scorers for weak models and refines the low-ambiguity limitation toward little benefit rather than failure. The original hallucination mechanism remains in Appendix D.

D1.justification: v2 documents the hyperparameter search grid, annotation instructions and annotator qualifications, and adds NLLB/Tower licenses. Software and A100 hardware disclosures are unchanged. Conversely, sequence-probability and BARTScore aggregation descriptions become less explicit.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects forced-decoding evaluation to Prism and prior NLLB scoring work. Related work substantially expands discussion of synthetic supervised QE, translation uncertainty and calibration, while Appendix F adds research context for practical QE applications and moderate correlations.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition. It separates the underconfidence investigation from the algorithm, reorganizes experimental discussion and moves the hallucination case to an appendix. The title and terminology also change throughout.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains a human-validity panel, and v2 adds annotation-form, tuning and correlation figures alongside new comparison and ablation tables. Dataset/model tables become single-column and scoring tables are redesigned. v1's hallucination Figure 5 moves to Appendix D as Figure 9.

improvement.justification: v1 inferred that dominant clusters contain valid alternatives without human verification. v2 directly investigates that premise and adds stronger comparator evaluations, sensitivity analyses, aggregation controls and metric/applicability checks, substantially strengthening validation of the unchanged method. The small annotation study, missing uncertainty estimates and less explicit aggregation descriptions remain limitations, but the added evidence materially improves the paper's empirical foundation.
